notes: Cover panel re-shoot of chandrama-09-pura: standing, full length, headroom for the tall crop.
prompt: Editorial fashion photograph for an Indian handloom label's festive lookbook. Tall vertical 9:16 frame.
GARMENT (a real product; match the reference photos exactly, including colours, borders and motifs):

- Saree: the olive-green tussar tissue silk saree from the first three references, woven with fine gold zari lines throughout that give a metallic shimmer, a plain gold zari pallu and small tassels. Crisp, luminous, slightly stiff drape.
- Blouse: the mustard-yellow silk brocade blouse from the last two references, elbow-length sleeves, round neckline.
- Pleated neatly, the gold pallu hanging straight from her left shoulder so the zari lines run unbroken.
MUSE: a woman in her mid-thirties with big natural curls, warm brown skin, a kundan choker, gold bangles, a radiant open smile, looking up at the moon.
MOMENT AND PLACE: Sharad Purnima on a whitewashed rooftop: a huge, luminous full moon in the deep blue sky above her, a wide brass urli of floating diyas and marigold petals at her feet.
LIGHT: Cool moonlight from behind as a rim light, warm diya glow from below on her face and the zari.
COVER FRAMING (this photograph becomes one tall, narrow panel of the lookbook's opening page, behind a large title):
- POSE: she is standing upright, full length, head to toe in frame; ignore any seated or kneeling pose mentioned above.
- HEADROOM: the top quarter of the frame is calm, empty background (sky, wall, foliage or soft darkness); her head sits about a quarter of the way down, never near the top edge.
- Subject centred horizontally and filling the middle third of the width, so a narrow vertical crop keeps all of her.
- Keep the background simple and softly out of focus; nothing busy behind her face.
- CAMERA: eye level, 50mm lens at f/2.8, gentle depth of field, medium-format look with fine grain.
